help.Arc Fail Timeout: How long to wait for the arc after the torch fires before giving up on this attempt (seconds).
help.Arc Maximum Starts: How many times to retry a failed arc start before pausing the program.
help.Arc OK High: Upper end of the voltage window that counts as a good arc. Mode 0 only — in modes 1 and 2 the arc-OK signal comes from the power supply.
help.Arc OK Low: Lower end of the voltage window that counts as a good arc. Mode 0 only.
help.Arc Restart Delay: How long to wait after a failed start before trying again (seconds).
help.Arc Voltage Offset: Shifts the arc voltage so it reads zero when there is no arc. Set with the torch off.
help.Arc Voltage Scale: Converts the raw arc-voltage input into real volts. Set with the torch running against a known voltage.
help.Float Switch Travel: How far the torch keeps travelling after the float switch trips — the difference between switch contact and real plate height.
help.Height Per Volt: How far the torch moves for each volt of arc error — the THC's scale. Depends on the process, not on preference.
help.Offset Feed Rate: How fast the machine moves when it has to travel to an offset probe position.
help.Ohmic Maximum Attempts: How many times to try the ohmic probe before falling back to the float switch.
help.Ohmic Probe Offset: Corrects for the ohmic probe sensing contact at a slightly different height than the true plate surface.
help.Pid D Gain: Damps the THC's response to a fast-changing error. Usually left at zero.
help.Pid I Gain: Corrects a height error that persists. Usually left at zero.
help.Pid P Gain: How hard the THC corrects a height error. Too low and it lags the plate, too high and it hunts.
help.Probe Feed Rate: How fast the torch descends while probing for the plate (machine units per minute).
help.Probe Start Height: Height above the work the torch drops to before it starts probing down.
help.Safe Height: The height rapids travel at, clear of anything clamped to the table.
help.Scribe Arming Delay: How long the scribe is armed before it is switched on, so the air has time to reach it (seconds).
help.Scribe On Delay: How long after the scribe switches on before motion begins (seconds).
help.Setup Feed Rate: How fast the torch moves between pierce height and cut height (machine units per minute).
help.Skip IHS Distance: Skip the height sense entirely if the next pierce is within this distance of the last cut, which saves time on close holes.
help.Slat Height: How far the slats stand above the table, so rapids stay above them.
help.Spotting Threshold: The arc voltage at which a spot is considered started and its timer begins (volts).
help.Spotting Time: How long the torch stays on after the threshold is reached. Milliseconds, not seconds.
help.THC Delay: How long after reaching cut feed rate before the THC starts correcting, so it ignores the pierce (seconds).
help.THC Sample Counts: How many arc-voltage samples must agree before automatic voltage takes them as the target.
help.THC Sample Threshold: How far apart those samples may be and still count as agreeing (volts).
help.THC Threshold: Voltage changes smaller than this are ignored, so the THC does not chase noise (volts).
help.Velocity Anti Dive Threshold: Below this share of the requested feed rate the THC freezes, so the torch does not dive into a corner (%).
help.Void Sense Slope: A rise this fast is read as the torch crossing a void, and the THC freezes rather than diving into it (volts/sec).
help.X Pierce Offset: Moves the pierce point off the cut line in X, so the pierce hole is not on the finished edge.
help.Y Pierce Offset: Moves the pierce point off the cut line in Y, so the pierce hole is not on the finished edge.
